failure: Dental Implant mechanical failure causing malfunction
constraint: Must maintain dental implant function within clinical specifications
mechanism: Poor prosthetic design is linked to peri-implantitis and peri-implant mucositis, which can lead to mechanical failure of the implant-prosthesis complex.
intervention: Redesign the implant abutment-prosthesis interface to eliminate subgingival cement retention and improve access for hygiene, using a screw-retained or cement-retained design with a polished, contoured emergence profile that minimizes biofilm accumulation.
expected_effect: Reduced peri-implant inflammation and mechanical stress concentration, thereby decreasing the incidence of prosthetic complications and maintaining implant function within clinical specifications.
falsification_test: In a simulated clinical trial, compare two implant groups (old vs. redesigned prosthetic design) over 12 months; measure peri-implant probing depths, bleeding on probing, and mechanical failure rates (screw loosening, fracture). The redesign is falsified if failure rates and inflammation markers are not significantly lower (p<0.05) than the old design.

source_evidence.source_title: From fixture to function: Evaluating prosthetic complications in dental implant rehabilitation.
source_evidence.source_span: Implant-supported prostheses are widely accepted treatment modalities for replacing missing teeth in partially or completely edentulous patients. Prosthetic complications in implant dentistry can be challenging for long-term success. Insufficient hygiene care, residual cement, and poor prosthetic design are issues linked to peri-implantitis and peri-implant mucositis.
